candidates.quote:
At 5:00 a.m. ET, on Wednesday, October 14, 2020, less than three weeks before the 2020 
presidential election, the New York Post published a potentially election-altering news story 
about a years-long influence peddling scheme carried out by the family of the Democratic 
nominee for president, former Vice President Joe Biden.2 The Post article detailed how Hunter 
Biden leveraged his famous last name to provide foreign officials with access to his father in 
exchange for the Biden family’s significant financial gain.3 This information was recovered from 
the hard drive of a laptop attributed to Hunter Biden, and the article included pictures of a signed 
federal subpoena, demonstrating that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had seized that 
hard drive.4 Neither Hunter Biden nor the Biden presidential campaign denied the allegations or 
the provenance of the laptop; indeed, the Biden Department of Justice (DOJ) has since 
authenticated the laptop as evidence in federal court.5

The FBI’s failure to alert social-media companies that the Hunter Biden laptop was real, and not mere Russian disinformation, is particularly troubling. The FBI had the laptop in their possession since December 2019 and had warned social-media companies to look for a “hack and dump” operation by the Russians prior to the 2020 election. Even after Facebook specifically asked whether the Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation, Dehmlow of the FBI refused to comment, resulting in the social-media companies’ suppression of the story. As a result, millions of U.S. citizens did not hear the story prior to the November 3, 2020 election.

**WASHINGTON, D.C.** – On July 17, 2023, the House Judiciary Committee and Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government conducted a transcribed interview of Laura Dehmlow, the Section Chief of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). During her transcribed interview, Dehmlow revealed that the same FBI personnel who were warning social media companies about a potential Russian “hack and leak” operation in the run-up to the 2020 election knew that the laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was not Russian disinformation. After the *New York Post* broke a story based on the contents of the laptop about Biden family influence peddling, the FBI made the institutional decision to refuse to answer direct questions from social media companies about the laptop’s authenticity—despite months of constant information sharing up to that time. Put simply, after the FBI conditioned social media companies to believe that the laptop was the product of a hack-and-dump operation, the Bureau stopped its information sharing, allowing social media companies to conclude that the *New York Post* story was Russian disinformation.

According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.

immediately, major social media platforms, including Twitter and Facebook—the modern-day

passages.P1: # Judge dismisses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe
passages.P3: by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk
passages.P6: FILE - Hunter Biden arrives for a closed-door deposition on Capitol Hill in Washington, Feb. 28, 2024. AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)
passages.P7: WASHINGTON (TNND) — A federal judge on Monday dismissed a criminal complaint accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, sharply criticizing the Justice Department’s handling of the case.
passages.P8: “What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in a ruling from the bench, according to The Associated Press.
passages.P9: Faruqui said prosecutors had not established probable cause to move forward with the charges against Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides. The Justice Department could still seek an indictment from a grand jury.
passages.P10: The judge pointed to the timing of the investigation, which an FBI agent testified began the day after President Donald Trump delivered a speech revisiting his 2020 election loss. The agent said FBI Director Kash Patel ordered the investigation and closely tracked its progress. He also testified he worried the inquiry could be viewed as political.
passages.P11: “I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend that I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said, referring to the decision to bring charges shortly before Tuesday’s midterm voting, the Associated Press reported.
passages.P12: Floris and Benavides were charged last month with making false statements to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into Hunter Biden. Both worked for the bureau’s now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, which monitored foreign interference campaigns.
passages.P13: According to the criminal complaint, Floris told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that she had not discussed Hunter Biden while assigned to the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI had Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia in 2023. Investigators alleged that records and communications contradicted their testimony. The two have denied wrongdoing, and the allegations had not been tested at trial.
passages.P14: The case also drew criticism from Faruqui over prosecutors’ decision to use a criminal complaint instead of seeking a grand jury indictment. Last week, the judge struck an amended complaint that prosecutors had filed overnight with an additional charge, saying it had not first been approved by the court.
passages.P15: The Justice Department’s allegations concerned statements the former officials made in 2023 about their knowledge of the laptop and the task force’s work. The department has argued that the officials’ testimony misled lawmakers investigating the FBI’s handling of information related to Hunter Biden.
passages.P16: The ruling is a setback for prosecutors, but it does not prevent them from presenting the allegations to a grand jury.
passages.P18: **Editor's note:** *The Associated Press contributed to this article.*
